 Judgment
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Suman Bainik in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2.

That, on 16.09.2022 at about 3.45 a.m, the deceased Suman Bainik was riding the Scooter bearing No.KA-50-X-8045, infront of Shell Petrol Bunk, Bellary Road, Near Sanjaynagar, Bangalore by taking U Turn, at that time, driver of Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB-1189 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that immediately after the accident, said Suman Bainik was shifted to Baptist Hospital and died in the hospital during the course of treatment.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital and the body was handed over to the petitioners.

The petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 22 years and working as a Helper at Thripureshwari Medical by earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing the entire income towards the welfare of the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have put to untold misery,
pain, shock and mental agony.
5. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB- 1189.
Hence, jurisdictional Sadashivanagar Traffic Police have filed criminal case in Cr.No.74/2022 against driver of said vehicle.
Hence, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 were appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.

In the written statement respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB-1189 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further contended that, driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. F.C. and permit to the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. The respondent No.2 in the written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further he has stated that, he is the RC owner of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP- 04-UB-1189 and got insured his vehicle with respondent No.1 the policy was in force as on the date of the accident and driver of said vehicle was having valid D.L.
Further contended that, accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Suman Bainik had died due to injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was infront of Shell Petrol Bunk,
Bellary Road, near Sanjaynagar, U Turn, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB- 1189 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3) What order or award?

ADDITIONAL ISSUES 1) Whether the respondents prove that this accident is due to fault of the deceased as stated in their written statement?

3 2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?

15. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB- 1189, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently
Suman Bainik had succumbed to the injuries.

16. On the other hand, the respondents have contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB-1189.
17.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
18. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Sri. Chandan Banik examined as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

Ex.P9-copy of charge sheet.

19. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Thanmay Kanthi Bhawnik, the S.H.O. of Sadhashivanagar Police has registered the case in Cr.No.74/2022 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86102509/

Upon the investigation the police have filed the charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under section 279,
304(A) of IPC and Section 185, 115, 117 of IMV Act.

20. PW1 was subjected for cross-examination at length, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
21. On the other hand, the respondents have examined Administrative officer of respondent No.1 as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
In his chief- examination RW1 has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
22. On perusal of Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar and sketch, it appears that accident took place at about 3.45 a.m., infront of Shell Petrol Bunk, Sanjaynagar U Turn, there is a way to reach Sanjaynagar.
The deceased was rode his two wheeler by using the said road.
So, it cannot be said that there is no way to cross the Hebbal, Mekhri main road.
The Lorry driver could have taken little bit of care and caution while driving the vehicle the accident would have avoided.
24. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has argued that deceased was rode the two wheeler by consuming alcohol.
Hence, negligence on the part of rider of two wheeler.

It is admitted fact the I.O.
has invoked Sec.115, 177 and 185 of IMV Act.
On perusal of FSL report attached with Ex.P8.
Post mortem
report

it appears that deceased was consumed alcohol and quantum of eithanal alcohol =
32 mg /100 ml blood, which is permissible quantity.
Therefore, it cannot be said that deceased was riding two wheeler rash and negligently by consuming alcohol.
On the other hand, due to accident the lorry took away two wheeler around 100 feet away from the accident place.
It shows that Lorry came in high speed and dashed to two wheeler which was crossing the road.
As a result of which, the deceased was sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries at hospital.

Further Ex.P9 charge sheet discloses that after the investigation I.O has filed charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and also against deceased person for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 of IPC and Sec. 115, 177 and 185 of IMV Act.

But the evidence placed before the Tribunal very well establishes that the accident took place on the negligence of driver of Lorry bearing No.AP-04-UB-1189.
23.
In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB-1189 and in the said accident, Suman Bainik succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative and Addl.
Issue No.1 in the Negative.

sentences.text:
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P10 to Ex.P12 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased, which have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak that the petitioners are the parents of the deceased.

25. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioners No.1 & 2 in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care from their son, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, at the time of cross-examination of the PW1.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
26. To prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident, the petitioners have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P12.
On going through same, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 16.03.2000.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
The alleged accident had occurred on 16.09.2022.

Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident,
the deceased was aged about 22 years.
For his age, multiplier '18' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
27. In connection with the work of the deceased in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as Helper and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The petitiners have not placed any document to prove the actual income of the deceased.

Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.
Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/- p.m., for the year 2022, which will meet the ends of justice.

28. Another point tobe taken into consideration herein that as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.

29. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
" It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

In case the deceased was self- Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86102509/
6 employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.

entities.text: Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50- 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

"
30. Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor,
deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 22 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "18" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein as on the date of the accident was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
And Rs.1,86,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,86,000+74,400)= Rs.2,60,400/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.1,30,200/- (Rs.2,60,400- Rs.1,30,200/-).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "18".
Which comes to Rs.23,43,600/-.

31 . Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following decision;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz.,
loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

32. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86102509/
7 of Rs.44,000/-
each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 & 2 under the head loss of filial consortium.

sentences.text: 33. The petitioners contended that, they have incurred huge amount towards medication of the deceased at the time of accident.
To prove the same, they have produced Ex.P14 medical bills.
There are no contra materials to disbelieve the said medical bills produced by the petitioners.
Therefore this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.33,180/- under the head medical expenses.
34. The petitioners contended that, they have incurred huge amount towards transportation dead body at the time of accident.
To prove the same, they have produced Ex.P15 transportation dead body and Ex.P16 reservation bills.
There are no contra materials to disbelieve the said bills produced by the petitioners.
Therefore this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.22,442/- under the head transportation of dead body.
35. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of Rs.23,43,600-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 88,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Medical expenses Rs. 33,180-00  Transportation dead body Rs. 22,442-00
Total Rs.25,20,222

. Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.25,20,222/-
(Rupees twenty five lakh twenty thousand two hundred and twenty two only), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text: As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-04-UB-1189 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
38. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 12.07.2022 to 11.07.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 16.09.2022.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative and Addl. Issue No.2 in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
39.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2 and Addl. Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,20,222/-(Rupees twenty five lakh twenty thousand two hundred and twenty two only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.

Out of share amount of petitoner No.1 and 2, 40% of the amount together with interest shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of of the amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86102509/
5 motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
26. To prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident, the petitioners have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P12.
Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.
Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/- p.m., for the year 2022, which will meet the ends of justice.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self- Chandan Banik vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86102509/
6 employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50- 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 22 years as on the date of the accident.

ISSUE No.3:
39.
In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2 and Addl. Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,20,222/-(Rupees twenty five lakh twenty thousand two hundred and twenty two only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.
Out of share amount of petitoner No.1 and 2, 40% of the amount together with interest shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of of the amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
